blocks.content: Metamorphic rocks are formed under the action of pressure, volume and temperature changes.

items: Direct matching questions on Parent Rock vs Metamorphic Rock (e.g., Clay/Shale to Slate, Sandstone to Quartzite) are extremely high-yield for SSC and UPSC Prelims.
Remember that Gneiss originates from Granite (Igneous), whereas Marble originates from Limestone (Sedimentary).
Differentiate between Foliated rocks (Slate, Schist, Gneiss) and Non-Foliated rocks (Marble, Quartzite).

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Metamorphic rocks form under the action of Pressure, Volume, and Temperature (PVT) changes on existing igneous or sedimentary rocks.
Thermal metamorphism occurs due to intense heat and is classified into Contact Metamorphism (localised magma contact) and Regional Metamorphism (large-scale tectonic forces).
Dynamic metamorphism involves restructuring and recrystallisation of rocks due to mechanical deformation without significant chemical alteration.
Foliation or Lineation is the structural arrangement of mineral grains or crystals in parallel layers or bands during metamorphism.
Banding refers to metamorphic rocks displaying alternating thin-to-thick layers of light and dark minerals.
